import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Read the data
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Age distribution
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']
ax1.hist(df['Age'], bins=20, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax1.set_xlabel('Age')
ax1.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax1.set_title('Age Distribution')
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 2. Income distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
df_income = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])
ax2.hist(df_income['Income'], bins=30, color='coral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax2.set_xlabel('Income')
ax2.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax2.set_title('Income Distribution')
ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 3. Education level
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
education_counts = df['Education'].value_counts()
ax3.bar(education_counts.index, education_counts.values, color='lightgreen', edgecolor='black')
ax3.set_xlabel('Education Level')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')
ax3.set_title('Education Distribution')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax3.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 4. Spending by category
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_totals = df[spending_cols].sum()
spending_totals.index = ['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold']
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(spending_totals)))
ax4.bar(spending_totals.index, spending_totals.values, color=colors, edgecolor='black')
ax4.set_xlabel('Product Category')
ax4.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax4.set_title('Total Spending by Product Category')
ax4.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 5. Marital Status
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
ax5.pie(marital_counts.values, labels=marital_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90)
ax5.set_title('Marital Status Distribution')

# 6. Purchase channels comparison
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
purchase_channels = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases', 'NumDealsPurchases']
channel_totals = df[purchase_channels].sum()
channel_totals.index = ['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store', 'Deals']
ax6.bar(channel_totals.index, channel_totals.values, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
ax6.set_xlabel('Purchase Channel')
ax6.set_ylabel('Total Purchases')
ax6.set_title('Purchases by Channel')
ax6.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 7. Income vs Total Spending scatter
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])
ax7.scatter(df_clean['Income'], df_clean['TotalSpending'], alpha=0.6, color='purple', edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
ax7.set_xlabel('Income')
ax7.set_ylabel('Total Spending')
ax7.set_title('Income vs Total Spending')
ax7.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 8. Campaign acceptance rate
ax8 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
campaign_cols = ['AcceptedCmp1', 'AcceptedCmp2', 'AcceptedCmp3', 'AcceptedCmp4', 'AcceptedCmp5', 'Response']
acceptance_rates = df[campaign_cols].mean() * 100
acceptance_rates.index = ['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response']
ax8.bar(acceptance_rates.index, acceptance_rates.values, color='salmon', edgecolor='black')
ax8.set_xlabel('Campaign')
ax8.set_ylabel('Acceptance Rate (%)')
ax8.set_title('Campaign Acceptance Rates')
ax8.grid(alpha=0.3, axis='y')

plt.suptitle('Customer Marketing Data Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
